Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the post-Lunch session. Pat Cummins leads his troops out to the centre. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul to open the innings for India. Mitchell Starc has the red cherry in hand and he is raring to go. Three slips and a gully await. Away we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

A lead of 46 runs may not seem massive in most Test matches, but on this challenging surface, it could prove invaluable. While Australia will be disappointed with their batting collapse, they know the game is far from over. The hosts will take heart from India's recent batting struggles, compounded by the inexperience in their lineup. With confidence low among the Indian batters, the Australian bowlers will be itching to exploit the conditions and claw their way back into the contest. With that said, join us at 5 am GMT for the post-Lunch session. Stay tuned.

So, the question now remains, has the pitch gotten better to bat on? Australia's impressive second-hour performance and successful reduction of the deficit, especially through the last-wicket stand, suggests more manageable batting conditions. While India might be frustrated by their inability to wrap up the innings quickly, they'll likely view the seemingly easier conditions as the ball got older as a positive sign for their own batting to come.

Earlier into the innings, Australia were rocked early with the Indian seamers running through the top order. Bumrah was the destructor in chief as he removed Khawaja, McSweeney, and Smith in quick intervals. Marnus Labuschagne scratched his first run after 24 deliveries but could only add a couple of runs. With trouble looming large, Australia desperately needed someone to sail their ship out of turbulent waters, but the Indian pacers just didn't give them any respite and utilized the conditions nicely. With Starc being the highest scorer for Aussies, it was Jasprit Bumrah who claimed his 11th five-wicket haul in Test career and was ably supported by Harshit Rana and Mohammed Siraj who shared the remaining five among them.

However, the final Australian pair of Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood showed gritty resistance, much to India's frustration. Their stubborn partnership grew steadily, with each run adding to the bowling side's anxiety. A dropped catch by Pant off Hazlewood's batting only added to India's growing concerns. Starc, in particular, displayed a good composure, handling the pace attack with efficiency. There were innumerable plays and misses with the ball flirting past the outside edge off Bumrah's bowling, but Starc looked a bit more comfortable against the others and truly maintained his ground for 112 deliveries, scoring a handy 26 runs, and was also the highest run scorer for the hosts. Hazlewood, too, showed a bit of resistance and the two added 25 runs together, battling it out for 110 deliveries.

Harshit Rana and Jasprit Bumrah began the day for India by constantly bashing those hard lengths and asking all the tough questions to the opposition batters. There was good carry and bounce which tested the batters' temperament. Bumrah made an immediate impact, claiming Alex Carey's wicket with a brilliant delivery in his very first over of the day. Carey, typically known for shepherding the tail effectively, couldn't extend his stay at the crease. Rana soon followed suit with a wicket of his own, leaving Australia in a precarious position and still trailing significantly.

Another immersive session of play has flown by in this West Test and we have seen it all - bowling brilliance in the first hour and a remarkable batting resilience in the next. But, ultimately it will be the tourists who will be the happier side of the two walking off for the Lunch break. They have prevented Australia from taking the lead and have an invaluable lead of 46 runs to build upon.

OUT! IN THE AIR...RISHABH PANT TAKES IT THIS TIME! Harshit Rana finally ends this frustrating 10th-wicket partnership and claims his third wicket. Rana steams in from around the stumps and hones in a fractionally fuller-length delivery, attacking the stumps. Mitchell Starc gets his front foot out of the way and creates room for himself. Goes for a big heave across but only manages to get a top edge. Skies it behind the wickets and swirls over the slip cordon. Virat Kohli prepares himself for the catch but it is Rishabh Pant who calls for his catch, locks his eyes on the ball, settles under it and takes it safely. India have bowled Australia out for 104 to gain a handy lead of 46 runs!

PITCH REPORT - Russel Arnold and Wasim Akram are inspecting the Day 2 Perth pitch. Arnold says it is clear and sunny and much warmer. Informs that Australia have used the heavy roller once again which means there will be plenty of bounce. Also reckons that due to the presence of grass, the pitch will be quicker than Day 1. Wasim Akram says there's still a lot of grass on the pitch and also says the Indian bowlers bowled really well yesterday and constantly hit that 6-meter mark. Adds that there are a few small visible cracks that could open up depending on how long the game goes on.

On the other hand, Australia will look to Alex Carey, who has a knack for batting smartly with the tail, to help bridge the gap to India’s first-innings total of 150. Carey’s recent form in the Sheffield Shield gives him added confidence, and the hosts will be hoping for another gritty knock from him. Day 2 promises to be as riveting as the first. Stay tuned as the first ball is not far away.

In response, Jasprit Bumrah spearheaded India’s spirited comeback with the ball. As the day wore on, the pitch seemed to quicken, aiding the Indian pacers. Mohammed Siraj and debutant Harshit Rana provided excellent support to leave the hosts reeling at 67/7, trailing by 83 runs at the close of play. After a night's rest, Bumrah and Co. will be fresh and determined to finish off the innings swiftly, ideally keeping the hosts under 100.

Despite winning the toss, India could only muster 150 in their first innings, with the Australian pacers asserting dominance. Josh Hazlewood was the standout, claiming four wickets, while his fellow quicks chipped in effectively. The innings wasn’t without controversy, as KL Rahul was adjudged caught behind in a contentious decision where the third umpire found the evidence conclusive enough to overturn the on-field call of not out.

Hello, one and all! After an enthralling ride on the opening day, it's time to buckle up and dive into what promises to be another captivating day of Test cricket here in Perth. Day 1 of the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy was nothing short of captivating, living up to all the pre-series expectations. It was a day dominated by the pacers, with a staggering 17 wickets tumbling, all claimed by the quicks.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, as we call it a day from this riveting first day of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy, the Perth Test sits delicately poised. India's next target will be the evergreen Alex Carey, whose lower middle-order heroics - including that match-defining 98 in Christchurch earlier this year - have often swung games Australia's way recently. As the weekend approaches, the action resumes on November 23, Saturday, at 2.20 am GMT, with our build-up kicking much earlier. This absorbing contest has already set the stage for what is to come in the Tests to follow ahead. Day 2 promises more of the same. Until then, cheers!

A similar trend was evident in Australia's innings as well, with the new ball doing all the damage. The batters struggled to cope with the nip and zip off the deck. The hosts have three wickets in hand now, and notably, 83 is Australia's lowest total against India in Test cricket. Will India restrict the hosts below that, or can Australia stage a thrilling comeback on Day 2? This storied rivalry's intensity ensures that anything can happen as we move forward.

So whom does this first day belong to? India? Australia? The pacers, to be very fair. But if we take a magnified look, India holds a slight upper hand as Australia's deficit still reads 83 runs with more than half of the side in the dugout already. A day of high-octane cricket saw both sides trade heavy punches - Hazlewood landed the first blow with a masterful 4-fer, demolishing India's lineup for a paltry 150, though debutant Nitish Kumar Reddy's gritty 41 and the Pant-Reddy's resistance offered minimal respite for the visitors. But just when Australia thought they had the upper hand and it was a good toss to lose, Indian skipper Bumrah unleashed his own brand of threatening bowling with a 4-wicket haul and the others too chipping in time.

Bumrah's fiery spell found perfect partners in Siraj and Harshit Rana, who kept the pressure cooking. Rana delivered a gem of a delivery to send the dangerous Travis Head packing, while Labuschagne found himself frozen in time - facing excruciatingly questioning 24 deliveries to scratch his first run. He was joined by the seasoned Mitchell Marsh who attempted to withstand the storm but couldn't extend his inning with Labuschagne too, following the suit sooner. After that, it all went from bad to worst for 'Straaya' as they were further damaged to 59/7, staring down at a scary all-out.

While India's batting lineup was consumed by the relentless Aussie pacers bossing up and reduced to 150, the tourists fought fire with fire, extinguishing Australia's top order. Jasprit Bumrah emerged as the chief destructor, unleashing a questioning spell that left the Aussie top order smouldering. His accuracy and movement proved too hot to handle as he single-handedly reduced Australia to 19/3, dashing the hopes of Khawaja, McSweeney, and Smith in quick succession.
